checked.comment: Generic structured stochastic MAB: finite arms, known Theta, known observation family nu and known reward map mu. structured_general with general_model_class fits. The lower-bound learner_knows (T, K, reward_family) is appropriate, and unique optimal arm is Assumption 1.
Bernoulli branch (Assumption 2). OSSB uses ln t, so it does not need T; learner_knows is consistent with the algorithm's inputs.
Gaussian branch with unit variance (Assumption 3). gaussian_known_variance is correct, and listing sigma as known is justified because the variance is fixed at 1.
Theorem 1: liminf R/ln T >= C(theta) for uniformly good algorithms. Mapping C(theta) to C_lin is correct. Regret is defined through the expected mu(x(t), theta), so pseudo_regret is right.

Theorem 2, Bernoulli case: limsup R/ln T <= C(theta) F(eps, gamma, theta) with eps < 1/|X|. The assumptions are listed correctly. The definition of F agrees with the proof's final bound (C + 2 eps psi)(1 + gamma). The algorithm uses ln t, so horizon 'anytime' is right.
Theorem 2, Gaussian case: the same expression and assumptions as r2, with unit-variance Gaussian observations.

summary: The extraction is accurate. It has the Graves–Lai-type lower bound (Theorem 1) and both observation-model branches of Theorem 2 (OSSB's asymptotic optimality), each with the right assumptions, setting mappings and registry id (ossb). The finite-time bound in Section 6 is not a separate formal statement and is properly mentioned in the notes. I found no errors and no missing formal results.
